summary: A plate cut across a small imported part gave up with 'loop not inside any face piece'. The part had a revolved face spanning most of a turn whose surface's seam (where its angle wraps from 2 pi to 0) lay inside the face. SolidCraft's earlier kernel followed each loop's boundary point by point in the surface's parameters and gave each angle within [0, 2 pi), so where a boundary crossed the seam its parameter polygon jumped by a period: the pieces' loops came out with the wrong area and sign, and the boolean refused. Geometry is the PR test's: a ring of rectangular section, radii 5 and 6 mm and 4 mm high, revolved 300 degrees about Z, intersected with the plate x, y -10..10, z 1..2. The PR's test re-parameterised each revolved surface so that its seam fell inside the face; SM_API builds the revolve's own surfaces, so here the ring is turned -50 degrees about Z, which puts angle 0 inside each revolved face, and a full turn is added, whose faces hold their seam by construction. Volumes are closed forms (a sector of an annulus times its height); only lumps and volume are expected. The tolerance is 0.01 mm^3, as in the other boolean cases.

cases.name: ring_300_alone
cases.note: Control: the 300 degree ring of rectangular section (radii 5 and 6, 4 high), not cut.

cases.name: plate_across_ring_300
cases.note: The ring from angle 0 to 300 degrees, intersected with a plate z 1..2 that crosses all four of its faces' lengths.

volume.formula: 300/360 * pi * (6^2 - 5^2) * 1 = 55/6 * pi (the PR test's expected value)

cases.name: plate_across_ring_300_over_angle_zero
cases.note: The same ring turned -50 degrees about Z, so it runs from -50 to 250 degrees and angle 0, where a revolved surface's angle wraps from 2 pi to 0, lies inside each revolved face: the PR's case.

cases.name: plate_across_full_ring
cases.note: A full turn: the ring is closed, so every revolved face holds its surface's seam.
